items.title: Accelerated optimization of gas diffusion electrodes for CO2 electrolyzers
items.abstract: We introduce AdaCarbon, a high-throughput automation system designed to accelerate the development of GDEs for CO2 electrolysis. AdaCarbon consists of seven collaborative robots that automate GDE fabrication, characterization, and zero-gap CO2 electrolysis testing. Using this platform, we fabricated and tested 90 GDEs with varying Cu–Ag metal compositions and Nafion-Sustainion ionomer bilayers to optimize ethylene production at 200 mA cm−2. Our results show that higher Cu and Nafion content increased ethylene selectivity by 5%–9%. Furthermore, AdaCarbon accelerates GDE development by a factor of three compared to manual workflows, demonstrating its potential to significantly enhance CO2 electrolysis research.

items.title: Autonomous control of quantum-confined CsPbBr3 nanoplatelets
items.abstract: Atomically thin perovskite nanoplatelets (NPLs) exhibit narrow, thickness-quantized emission suited for color-pure optoelectronics and quantum-photonic technologies, yet reproducibly targeting a single thickness remains challenging because growth occurs within ultranarrow kinetic windows. Here, we introduce an autonomous fluidic lab that identifies and optimizes monolayer-controlled CsPbBr3 NPLs by integrating modular microfluidics, multi-modal in-line spectroscopy, and multi-objective Bayesian optimization. Closed-loop campaigns discover high-temperature synthesis routes that produce NPLs with user-defined emission targets while maximizing the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) and minimizing emission linewidth. A probabilistic digital twin maps how synthesis parameters cooperatively control quantum confinement, thickness dispersity, and radiative performance, revealing discrete growth regimes rather than a continuous trajectory. This framework autonomously identifies high-quality NPLs and nanocubes spanning the blue-green spectrum (455–520 nm) with narrow emission and high PLQY up to ∼98%, while translating the discovered routes to steady-state continuous-flow operation (19–41 mL hr-1) without loss of spectral fidelity.

items.title: Embodied intelligence in biosensors: From biological inspiration to AI integration
items.abstract: The convergence of microelectronics, synthetic biology, artificial intelligence (AI), and neuroscience is transforming biosensors into sophisticated systems for embodied intelligence (EI). Moving beyond simple detection, these advanced biosensors integrate sensing, storage, and processing, enabling human-like perception with immense application potential in healthcare, agriculture, and monitoring. This review highlights the essential role of advanced biosensors in realistic sensing and interaction. We explore how biological principles inspire artificial sensing designs and examine bioinspired sensory systems that combine biosensing with neuromorphic computing and multisensory fusion for efficient real-time environmental interaction. Additionally, we discuss the cutting-edge integration of sensory organoids with AI-driven computation, creating biohybrid systems that merge biological and artificial perception. These biohybrid systems increasingly blur the boundaries between biological and artificial perception, enabling the creation of truly intelligent, self-adaptive sensing platforms.

items.title: Knowledge-driven autonomous materials research via collaborative multi-agent and robotic system
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide new possibilities for accelerating materials research, yet their application in complex materials science remains limited. Here, we developed the collaborative multi-agent and robot system (MARS), a knowledge-driven hierarchical architecture coordinating 19 LLM agents with 16 domain-specific tools for closed-loop autonomous materials discovery. MARS combines scientific knowledge with decision-making capabilities while mitigating hallucination through retrieval-augmented generation with a customized knowledge base. In experimental validation, the system optimized perovskite nanocrystal synthesis within 10 iterations and designed a biomimetic “core-shell-corona” structure for water-stable perovskite composites in 3.5 h versus conventional methods requiring 4–6 months. This acceleration automates literature review and experimental planning, allowing researchers to focus on creative thinking while interacting through a natural language interface. This work establishes an integrated AI-driven framework for accelerating materials innovation and presents a paradigm for AI-enabled scientific discovery.

items.title: Toward a composable, modular laboratory ecosystem for autonomous materials research and development
items.abstract: Autonomous and automated experimentation have demonstrated the possibility of accelerating materials research and development by orders of magnitude. However, the investment in both time and money to design and build these platforms has proven to be a major roadblock in their adoption. This cost is driven by the bespoke nature of these platforms, requiring redundant engineering due to the complexity of handling multiple interfaces from multiple vendors. To mitigate these challenges, we suggest the development of a set of community-driven interchange standards for both hardware and software, allowing these platforms to be rapidly constructed from off-the-shelf modular components which can each be designed and built by multiple vendors. This would enable the creation of an autonomous materials research ecosystem.

items.title: Enhancing battery anomaly detection via trend-reversal spectrograms and multi-modal cross-attention
items.abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have attracted growing attention in recent years due to their potential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. However, anomaly detection in EV battery data remains challenging because of fluctuations, noise, and the inherent complexity of operational signals. In this study, we propose a deep learning-based, multi-modal anomaly detection framework to address these challenges. Specifically, we demonstrate that the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) can be applied to capture signal “trend reversals” in sequential data, providing additional information for anomaly detection. Building on this insight, we introduce a multi-modal architecture that integrates spectrogram and time-series representations to improve the discriminability of reconstruction errors between normal and abnormal samples. Furthermore, we propose a dual-branch detection strategy with logical fusion, leveraging both reconstruction-based and classification-based approaches. In addition, a cross-brand adaptive model is developed to transfer knowledge across EV brands, enabling deployment in new domains where only normal (unlabeled-anomaly) data are available. Experimental results on a large-scale real-world EV dataset demonstrate an average F1 score of 0.8667 and AUROC of 0.9485, outperforming existing methods. These results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed framework and highlight its potential for practical deployment in the EV industry.

items.title: Advances in AI-enhanced model predictive control for heat pumps: A comprehensive review
items.abstract: This review critically evaluates the effectiveness and feasibility of AI-driven model predictive control (AI-MPC) for heat-pump (HP) demand management across building and district scales. The recent studies from field trials, simulations, and comparative analyses consistently demonstrate that AI-MPC achieves significant energy and cost savings compared to rule-based control (RBC). Furthermore, AI-MPC delivers performance comparable to physics-based MPC, while surrogate and approximate controllers achieve these benefits with substantially reduced modeling complexity and computational runtime. The literature reveals key improvements, including energy and cost reductions ranging from 25% to 60% in representative AI-MPC applications. The district-level artificial neural network MPC (ANN-MPC) has been shown to reduce backup electric energy use by up to 71% relative to rule-based strategies. In residential and commercial contexts, the improvements range from 10 to 30%, with higher gains under load-shifting. MPC coordinating HP with thermal storage achieves 27.1% electricity cost savings under time-of-use pricing and 4.8–7.5% annual performance factor gains over RBC. At the residential scale, AI-assisted controls deliver 21–44% energy savings and 22–86% comfort improvements compared to conventional methods. AI-MPC feasibility depends on high-resolution data, privacy-preserving learning, and integration with building management systems. Overall, the review shows that AI-MPC can enable cost-optimal HP operation and grid-supportive flexibility on a scale, if challenges in data quality, system integration, and robustness are effectively addressed.

items.title: Applications and prospects of AI/ML in electric vehicle regenerative braking systems: A review
items.abstract: In response to global energy shortages and environmental pollution, electric vehicles (EVs) have emerged as a vital means of green transportation. Their energy utilization efficiency and driving range have become key research priorities. The regenerative braking system (RBS) enhances EV energy economy by recovering kinetic energy during braking. The recovered energy is converted into electrical energy and stored in the battery, making RBS a core vehicle energy-saving technology. This study reviews the current status and development trends of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) applications in electric vehicle regenerative braking control systems within the context of intelligent vehicle systems. First, the basic structure and operating principles of RBS are introduced. The technical characteristics of electric motors, energy storage devices, and friction brake actuators are then discussed, together with their integration methods in different EV architectures. Subsequently, intelligent control strategies based on supervised learning, unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, and deep learning are analyzed from three dimensions: energy recovery optimization, braking stability, and driving comfort. Their advantages over conventional methods are compared in terms of control logic, performance, adaptability, and system integration. The reviewed studies indicate that intelligent methods demonstrate significant potential in multi-objective coordination, dynamic condition adaptation, and cross-system integration. However, challenges remain in actuator coordination, communication latency, energy storage system durability, and safety validation. Finally, future research directions for RBS in intelligent vehicle systems are discussed, providing guidance for the development of efficient, safe, and comfortable regenerative braking technologies for EVs.

items.title: Multi-energy load forecasting incorporating AI algorithms: research status and trends in integrated energy systems
items.abstract: Against the background of accelerated transformation of the global energy structure towards decarbonization and cleanliness, Integrated Energy Systems (IES) has achieved rapid development, but at the same time, it is also facing a number of challenges and problems that need to be solved. High-precision multi-energy load forecasting, as the basic guarantee for stable operation and demand response of IES system, has become a hot direction of current research. This study aims to sort out and analyze the research lineage and development trend of multi-energy load forecasting in the context of IES. First, the development history and research hotspots of multi-energy load forecasting were reviewed by analyzing the keyword co-occurrence of related literature with the help of CiteSpace software. Second, it systematically summarizes the latest progress in the application of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms in this field, focuses on the analysis of methods and techniques to improve the prediction accuracy, and explores the coupling relationship and interdependence mechanism between different energy loads. It has been shown that feature extraction, data preprocessing, and model optimization strategies play a key role in improving prediction performance. Finally, this paper further explores the potential and application prospects of emerging AI methods in addressing the challenges of multi-energy load forecasting in IES, providing theoretical support and reference directions for related research.

items.title: Review of model-driven and data-driven/AI approaches for estimating frequency dynamics after a disturbance
items.abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources (RESs) through power electronic converters and inverters (PECIs) in modern power systems has led to a consistent decrease in system inertia, which poses significant challenges for managing and stabilizing complex frequency dynamics. Consequently, maintaining frequency stability and ensuring the security of the power grid have become critical issues. Addressing these issue requires the development of appropriate methods that accurately capture the complex frequency dynamics introduced by RESs. This review comprehensively surveys the changes in frequency dynamics following the integration of RESs and focuses on modeling, analysis, and application. The basic properties of system inertia, variations in inertia contributions across different power systems, effects of RES integration in different frequency-response stages, and current mainstream methods for estimating frequency dynamics are reviewed systematically. Essential data, algorithms, and software requirements are analyzed and a hybrid framework based on Improved System Frequency Response–Multi-scale Convolution Layer Improved Transformer (ISFR-MCIT) that integrates model-driven and data-driven approaches to enhance estimation accuracy in low-inertia systems is proposed. Case studies reveal that the proposed methods achieve a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0006 Hz for frequency nadir and 0.0016 s for nadir time validated in the Chinese Society for Electrical Engineering - Frequency Stability (CSEE-FS) test system, outperforming existing models by up to 60 % in accuracy metrics under varying scenarios. Finally, an outlook is provided on the quantitative assessment of frequency security and response, alongside the development of an equivalent inertia assessment system for future research.

items.title: Utilizing large-scale foundation models for prognostics and health management in wind turbines: Techniques, challenges, and future directions
items.abstract:
The Paris Agreement has catalyzed global green development, accelerating progress in wind energy. In 2024, new global wind turbine installations totaled 117 GW, raising the cumulative capacity to 1136 GW. As wind turbine deployment rapidly expands, prognostics and health management (PHM) becomes essential for ensuring safe, reliable, and stable operations. Large-scale foundation models (LSF-Models), such as ChatGPT, hold significant potential for enhancing wind turbine PHM. However, research on LSF-Models in wind turbine PHM remains limited. This paper aims to bridge this gap by systematically analyzing recent advancements, technologies, challenges, and future directions in this area. It provides an in-depth review of wind turbine PHM methods and a comprehensive collection of publicly available datasets. The paper also outlines the core LSF-Model frameworks and representative models. Applications of LSF-Models in wind turbine PHM, such as condition monitoring and anomaly detection, fault diagnosis, remaining useful life prediction, and maintenance decision-making, are discussed. Additionally, the paper examines key technologies, including multimodal alignment and fusion, fine-tuning of LSF-Models, integration with local knowledge bases, and intelligent agent technologies. Finally, it addresses the challenges of applying LSF-Models to wind turbine PHM and suggests potential future research directions. In the era of artificial general intelligence, LSF-Models are poised to revolutionize wind turbine PHM, optimizing traditional methods and unlocking new development opportunities.

items.title: AI awakens food packaging: Integrative advances, challenges, and future perspectives
items.abstract:
Background
Growing concerns about food safety, environmental sustainability, and consumer expectations are driving the transition from conventional passive packaging to active systems. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative tool to enhance food packaging by enabling data-driven design, real-time monitoring, and predictive quality control, thereby reducing food waste and supporting circular economy goals.
Scope and approach
This review provides a comprehensive and integrative analysis of AI-enabled innovations in food packaging. It introduces key AI technologies—including machine learning, deep learning, and generative models—and explores their applications across nine critical domains: material design and optimization, food safety and freshness monitoring, chemical migration and toxicity prediction, packaging process automation, supply chain and logistics optimization, personalized packaging design, recycling and waste reduction, carbon footprint assessment, and information and traceability systems. In addition, this review identifies the main technical, regulatory, economic, and consumer-related challenges and proposes future research directions to guide the transition from laboratory research to commercial implementation.
Key findings and conclusions
AI has demonstrated exceptional potential to improve packaging material performance, enable intelligent spoilage and quality monitoring, ensure chemical safety, and optimize manufacturing and supply chains. However, barriers such as limited data availability, complex regulatory requirements, high implementation costs, and the need for greater consumer trust remain significant. Future research should prioritize developing advanced materials for complex food systems, biodegradable and recyclable sensor platforms, interpretable and energy-efficient AI models, standardized evaluation frameworks, and strategies for economic feasibility and consumer engagement. Overall, AI-enabled intelligent packaging offers a promising pathway to achieving safe, smart, and sustainable food systems.

items.title: AI in cheese manufacturing: A comprehensive review of technologies, applications, and future prospects
items.abstract:
Background
Cheese, as a fermented dairy product, evolves a complex production process including milk standardization, pasteurization, fermentation, curdling, maturation, and packaging. These processes require precise control of key parameters such as pH, temperature, time, and microbial activity, while traditional methods often struggle to balance efficiency and consistency. In recent years, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into food processing has shown great potential to optimize the entire cheese production chain, from formulation design to safety assurance and quality control.
Scope and approach
This review first outlines key AI technologies, including data acquisition, data preprocessing, machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), natural language processing (NLP), and large language models (LLMs). It then systematically analyzes the current applications and challenges of AI across the cheese production chain, covering raw material inspection, formulation optimization, process control, quality evaluation, and packaging. In addition, AI-driven transformation pathways for cheese production and quality management are discussed, along with future perspectives.
Key findings and conclusions
The results indicate that AI enables real-time monitoring and intelligent control of critical parameters throughout the production process. Under laboratory conditions, this approach performs exceptionally well, with over half of the studies reporting classification accuracies exceeding 90% and regression models achieving R2 values above 0.9. However, challenges remain in real-world industrial deployment, including limited generalizability, high implementation costs, and low interpretability. Future advances in multimodal integration, edge intelligence, human–machine collaboration, and green manufacturing are expected to drive the cheese industry toward customized, low-carbon, and fully intelligent production systems.

Key challenges include data standardization, cybersecurity, and ethical AI considerations, while emerging approaches such as edge computing and blockchain-enhanced security offer promising solutions. The review also highlights the transition toward cognitive twin ecosystems in Industry 5.0-enabled agri-food systems, supporting cross-disciplinary collaboration and innovation. By synthesizing current research and identifying gaps, this study provides guidance for implementing DTs to enhance resilience, traceability, and digital transformation in modern food processing.

items.title: From biomimetics to AI-guided rational design: Four-component cell-wall-derived films for fresh horticultural produce with bidirectional humidity-gas modulation
items.abstract:
Background
Postharvest losses of fruits and vegetables, driven by their high moisture content and active metabolism, remain a critical challenge for global food sustainability. Conventional packaging lacks sufficient dynamic adaptability, often resulting in either overprotection (condensation, anaerobic respiration) or under protection (dehydration, wilting).
Scope and approach
This paper reviews a biomimetic strategy for reconstructing plant cell wall structures using cellulose, hemicellulose, pectin and lignin to fabricate composite film materials for intelligent packaging. Component recombination can be achieved via solution casting, electrospinning and other advanced film-forming technologies. The as-prepared biomimetic films can synergistically regulate multiple properties, including gas exchange, water vapor transport and antibacterial performance. Especially for intelligent upgrading, artificial intelligence technology can be used for big-data modeling and intelligent optimization of film-forming process parameters, structure-performance relationships and fresh-keeping adaptability of films. This approach overcomes the empirical limitations of traditional preparation processes and enables the precise, intelligent and customized development of biomimetic packaging materials.
Key findings and conclusions
These fully bio-based and biodegradable films offer a sustainable alternative to mitigate microplastic pollution from conventional petroleum-derived plastics. However, their industrial-scale adoption remains constrained by challenges in large-scale manufacturability, cost-effectiveness, and wet-state mechanical durability. Nonetheless, cell wall biomimetic films signify a paradigm shift from passive barrier materials to responsive intelligent packaging platforms. In the short term, they hold great promise for high-value perishable commodities; in the longer term, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven process optimization (reducing formulation screening experiments by 60–80%) and closed-loop sensing systems may further accelerate their commercialization.

items.title: From detection chains to prevention trends: An AI governance framework for terrestrial and marine food-safety systems
items.abstract:
Background
Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are fundamentally transforming food safety from reactive contamination detection toward predictive prevention systems, yet their deployment encounters governance deficits that threaten equitable adoption.
Scope and approach
This paper analyses 1766 publications (2015–2025) to evaluate AI detection systems, predictive analytics, and blockchain traceability across terrestrial and marine supply chains.
Key findings and conclusions
Computer vision achieves 95–99 % accuracy in pathogen detection, while blockchain enables traceability from days to seconds. Our analysis reveals a critical technology-to-governance imbalance (ratio 7.5:1) and severe under-representation of marine systems (terrestrial dominance 2.3:1; IUU-fishing research deficit 57:1), even though aquatic foods provide 17 % of global animal protein to 3.3 billion people. Fragmented regulatory frameworks across the European Union, the United States and the Asia-Pacific region create deployment uncertainty, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises. Marine food systems remain critically underserved despite their contribution to global animal protein, and governance fails to adequately address harmful algal blooms, heavy-metal bioaccumulation, and illegal fishing. We propose an AI governance framework for terrestrial and marine food-safety systems that incorporates adaptive regulatory mechanisms.

items.title: From detection to prevention: A cyber-secure AI ecosystem for mitigating milk adulteration and dairy fraud
items.abstract:
Background
The global dairy industry faces persistent and evolving threats from milk adulteration and fraudulent practices, which jeopardize public health, economic stability, and consumer trust. Conventional detection methods are reactive and increasingly inadequate, necessitating a paradigm shift towards preemptive prevention.
Scope and approach
This review critically examines the potential of a cyber-secure AI ecosystem, an integrated framework that progressively fuses Artificial Intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity to transform the dairy supply chain through seamless technical integration. We analyze how AI-driven methodologies, such as machine learning (ML) for non-linear pattern recognition, spectroscopic analysis for chemical profiling, and computer vision (CV) for visual inspection, are unified with cybersecurity measures via specific interfaces like secure Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) for Internet of Things (IoT) data ingestion and blockchain smart contracts for data validation. This enables encrypted data flows from supply chain sensors (capturing temperature, geolocation, and compositional profiles) to AI models, with feedback mechanisms, such as predictive anomaly alerts and adaptive model retraining, ensuring continuous system resilience and end-to-end data integrity, moving beyond isolated technologies to a cohesive ecosystem.
Key findings and conclusions
Our synthesis demonstrates that this deep integration creates a robust, multi-layered defense system where AI's predictive analytics are fortified by cybersecurity's protective protocols, enabling forensic attribution through immutable audit trails and a decisive transition from detection to prevention. For example, real-time IoT data, secured by zero-trust architectures, feeds into AI models for adulterant detection, with feedback loops triggering automated responses like data quarantines or model updates via federated learning, ensuring dynamic system adaptability. However, this paradigm shift faces significant hurdles, including the black box nature of complex AI models, the cost and scalability of blockchain, and socio-technical adoption barriers. We conclude that the strategic implementation of this ecosystem, while not a panacea, is critical for safeguarding public health and ensuring dairy industry integrity. The review provides a cohesive roadmap for stakeholders, emphasizing collaborative governance, standardized protocols, and emerging technologies like federated learning and quantum-resistant encryption to overcome existing barriers and build a resilient supply chain.

items.title: Multimodal nondestructive sensing and digital-twin-enabled quality control in soybean foods: A process-state-oriented review
items.abstract:
Background
Soybean foods are manufactured through tightly coupled operations in which raw-material heterogeneity is amplified into variation in extraction yield, gel structure, water state, flavor, and shelf-life performance. Although recent reviews have addressed individual sensing modalities or broader digitalization concepts, a soybean-specific synthesis is still lacking on how sensing can make quality-forming process states observable and support auditable, bounded intervention in real manufacturing environments.
Scope and approach
This review examines multimodal nondestructive sensing for soybean foods across receiving, extraction, gelation, fermentation, and storage. It prioritizes soybean-direct evidence for near-infrared spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging, Raman spectroscopy and surface-enhanced Raman scattering, machine vision, low-field nuclear magnetic resonance, physical-field sensing, and biomimetic flavor sensors, while using related food-engineering literature to contextualize unresolved issues in model transfer, sensor drift, fusion benchmarking, edge deployment, digital-twin synchronization, and control-oriented validation. Given the diversity of matrices, labels, sensors, and validation designs, the review adopts a process-state-to-action synthesis rather than pooling performance metrics, and considers how soft sensing, deployable AI, and hybrid digital twins support action-relevant state estimation in soybean manufacturing.
Key findings and conclusions
Multimodal sensing can move soybean quality control from endpoint inspection toward prediction-guided intervention by revealing composition, structural evolution, moisture migration, spatial heterogeneity, and flavor dynamics in real time. Its practical value depends on building verifiable mappings between sensing proxies and latent quality states and linking these states to bounded actions. Current soybean-direct evidence supports process-state observability and human-supervised decision support more strongly than autonomous closed-loop control. Future work should prioritize standardized state definitions, soybean-direct datasets with rich metadata, fusion benchmarking against single-modality baselines, calibration transfer, drift-aware model governance, cost-tiered edge deployment, and human-supervised digital-twin workflows. A staged pathway from offline prediction to online soft sensing, bounded intervention, and eventually constrained closed-loop control with explicit safety and quality limits offers the most credible route toward deployable soybean-food quality management.

items.title: PRPP allocation-centered microbial biomanufacturing of Nucleosides: Metabolic engineering, AI-DBTL, and food-grade industrialization challenges
items.abstract:
Background
Nucleosides and their derivatives are essential functional nutrients for maintaining physiological homeostasis, with significant roles in immune regulation, gut health, and anti-fatigue; they therefore hold broad potential for application in dietary supplements and functional foods. Developing efficient and green microbial biomanufacturing processes is consequently a critical objective for meeting market demand.
Scope and approach
This review systematically analyzes recent advances in nucleoside biomanufacturing, encompassing strategies of strain mutagenesis, genome editing, and metabolic pathway engineering. It details the intracellular biosynthetic pathways of pyrimidine and purine nucleosides and their key regulatory nodes, with a particular focus on 5-phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate (PRPP) as the central metabolic hub for precursor allocation and flux control. Multi-scale metabolic engineering approaches such as precursor enhancement, feedback inhibition alleviation, degradation pathway blocking, cofactor balancing, and transporter modification. The application of artificial intelligence is integrated with multi-omics data for enzyme rational design, metabolic bottleneck identification, and fermentation control is also examined.
Key findings and conclusions
Current fermentation titers for uridine, cytidine, and inosine have reached 70.3 g/L, 18.3 g/L, and 25.8 g/L, respectively, demonstrating the considerable industrial potential of microbial synthesis. However, single-point modifications frequently induce systemic imbalances, including redox disruption, increased metabolic burden, and reduced stability during scale-up. The integration of artificial intelligence with automated biofoundries has the potential to accelerate strain iteration and process optimization by establishing a design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycle, but its practical feasibility in nucleoside production still requires experimental validation and industrial-scale studies. Future research could achieve further breakthroughs in dynamic flux regulation, PRPP allocation engineering, and industrial robustness design to advance functional nucleoside production toward higher yields, lower costs, and wider applications.

items.title: Accurate prediction of high-temperature ionic melt viscosity through data-driven modeling enhanced with explainable AI
items.abstract: The increasing demand for high-performance steels and environmentally sustainable pyrometallurgical processes has led to significant compositional variations in ionic melts and the development of novel fluxes. Optimizing ionic melt performance requires precise control of thermophysical properties, with viscosity being a key factor influencing heat and mass transport in various industrial applications. However, traditional experimental and analytical methods are often cost-prohibitive and pose challenges in generalizing findings across diverse compositions and temperatures. This study introduces MOVINet (MOlten ions VIscosity Network), a data-driven modeling framework designed to predict high-temperature ionic melt viscosity based on melt composition, temperature, and fundamental properties of 13 components, including 12 oxides and one fluoride. Trained on 1981 experimentally measured data points and evaluated using 480 independent data points, MOVINet achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.1480, reducing error by 57.7 % compared to the best existing model (MAE = 0.3497). It consistently demonstrated high accuracy across six ionic melt types over a broad temperature range (1100–1870 °C) and maintained low errors even for melts containing previously unseen components (e.g., MAEs of 0.0567 for CaCl2 and 0.1463 for BaO-containing samples). Furthermore, explainable AI analysis confirmed the dominant influence of temperature while highlighting compositional features affecting viscosity.

items.title: A Semantic Representation learning perspective-based approach for multimodal science question answering
items.abstract: Multimodal science question answering performs multimodal learning and logical reasoning based on given visual and text input to answer science questions. For a particular input pair, visual and text express the common semantic meaning through different modal carriers. The semantic meanings expressed by the visual and text modal carriers sourcing different pairs are independent. However, the high entanglement between modal and semantic representation and the weak semantic differences between different pairs hinder the learning of visual and text semantic representation. In this work, we introduce a semantic representation learning perspective-based approach (SRLP) for multimodal science question answering. First, we maximize the matching degree between visual and text semantic representations within the particular pair by disentanglement and agreement constraints. At the same time, we combine contrastive learning with disentangled representation learning to enhance the cross-modal semantic representation learning of the particular pair. The learned cross-modal semantic representation is finally fed into the decoder to generate the answer text. Experiments on two multimodal science question answering datasets demonstrate the excellent performance of SRLP, proving the effectiveness of cross-modal agreement and contrastive learning. Data and source code are available at https://github.com/gaoling-code/SRLP.

items.title: A hierarchical information policy fusion framework with multimodal large language models for autonomous guidewire navigation in endovascular procedures
items.abstract: Robotic-assisted endovascular interventions promise to transform cardiovascular therapy by improving procedural precision and minimizing cardiologists’ exposure to occupational risks. However, current systems are limited by their reliance on manual control and lack of adaptability to complex vascular anatomies. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Hierarchical Autonomous Guidewire Navigation and Delivery (HAG-ND) framework that leverages the strengths of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and a novel reinforcement learning module inspired by Deep Q-Networks (DQNs). The high-level MLLM is trained on diverse blood vessel and guidewire scenarios from various angles and positions, enabling it to assess the suitability and timing of substance release at the target location. Within the MLLM, a parliamentary mechanism is introduced, where multiple specialized models, each focusing on a specific aspect of the vascular environment, vote on the optimal course of action. The low-level reinforcement learning module focuses on optimizing autonomous guidewire navigation to the designated target site by learning from the rich semantic understanding provided by the MLLM. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the HAG-ND framework significantly improves the accuracy and reliability of guidewire positioning and targeted delivery compared to existing methods. By harnessing the complementary capabilities of MLLMs and novel reinforcement learning techniques in a hierarchical architecture, HAG-ND represents a significant step towards fully autonomous and adaptive robotic-assisted endovascular interventions.

items.title: A robust and efficient deep optimization network for spatiotemporal data fusion
items.abstract: Satellites strive to strike a delicate balance between temporal and spatial resolution, thereby rendering the achievement of high resolution in both aspects challenging. Spatiotemporal fusion algorithms have emerged as a promising solution to tackle this challenge. However, with changes in spatiotemporal conditions, existing spatiotemporal fusion methods, particularly those based on deep learning, face challenges such as decreased prediction accuracy and poor reconstruction accuracy in areas of abrupt changes. This presents significant challenges for the fusion of multi-source remote sensing data to generate cloud-free remote sensing images on a daily scale. In this context, the study proposes a multiscale Attention-Guided deep optimization network for Spatiotemporal Data Fusion (AGSDF) method. The algorithm is designed to generate daily fine images using coarse image, based on historical reference fine images. Specifically, it firstly attempts to use a physical attention mechanism to mitigate the effects of climate change in time-series images. Implementing a continuous spatiotemporal fusion process across multiple scales significantly enhances the model's robustness. The performance of AGSDF was evaluated and compared to nine methods at six sites worldwide. The experimental results indicate that AGSDF achieved a top score in the assessment. Consequently, AGSDF holds high potential to produce accurate remote sensing products with high temporal and spatial resolution across extensive regions.

items.abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) capture extensive multimodal information, such as clinical narratives, imaging, physiological waveforms and laboratory results, yielding richly detailed yet heterogeneous portraits of patient status. Leveraging these complementary sources is pivotal for precision medicine, and recent advances in multimodal machine learning have made such integration increasingly tractable. We present a critical survey of multimodal learning for healthcare, organized around the predominant “text + X” paradigm that arises because imaging, waveform and laboratory findings are routinely encoded or summarized in free-text reports (e.g., radiology or ECG summaries). From this vantage, we review: representation learning, fusion strategies, and clinical downstream tasks, highlighting how each technical choice aligns or conflicts with the underlying semantics and statistical properties of the modalities involved. Throughout, we emphasize concepts such as cross-modal semantic consistency (e.g., lesion descriptors matching visual regions) and modality-specific noise characteristics, drawing connections to current modeling techniques. By exposing mismatches between data properties and algorithmic assumptions, we outline open challenges and propose directions toward more unified, clinically deployable multimodal frameworks. Addressing these gaps, we argue, is essential for translating methodological innovation into reliable decision support systems in real-world medical settings.

items.title: ASAC-Net: A novel multimodal alignment-complementary fusion framework for EEG-fNIRS emotion recognition
items.abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology enables the widespread use of electroencephalography (EEG) in emotion recognition, as it directly captures brain neural activity and reflects emotional states. However, unimodal EEG provides limited information, so functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is introduced to compensate for the limitations of unimodal data through multimodal fusion, leading to improved recognition performance. In this study, we first build an EEG-fNIRS emotion dataset using a virtual reality (VR) active interaction paradigm involving 21 participants. We then propose an Adaptive Spatial Alignment-Complementary Network (ASAC-Net) for EEG-fNIRS based emotion recognition. Specifically, to extract spatial features from each modality, we introduce an intra-modal encoding module based on adaptive graph convolution. In the fusion phase, contrastive learning aligns EEG and fNIRS representations, while a Cross-Modal Transformer enhanced by adjacent aggregation position encoding captures complementary features. Finally, emotion classification is performed using a dynamic routing mechanism. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves 80.52% accuracy on the self-built dataset for cross-subject emotion recognition, outperforming state-of-the-art multimodal baselines. Ablation experiments verify the effectiveness of each module. Furthermore, extensive evaluations on three public single-modal datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms multiple existing unimodal baselines. In terms of interpretability, brain connectivity patterns learned by the model align with neuroscience evidence in frontal and occipital regions. Additionally, cross-modal attention reveals distinct brain region engagement across emotions.

items.title: An enhanced 3D U-Net with multi-level information fusion for real-time CO2 field inference of coal-fired boiler
items.abstract: Accurate acquisition of the CO2 spatial distribution in coal-fired boilers is of great importance for combustion state perception, carbon emission assessment and low-carbon operation. However, direct measurement remains challenging due to limited sensor coverage and highly complex internal conditions. Although CFD can provide high-fidelity numerical analysis results, its high computational cost limits real-time applicability. Accordingly, a multi-level information fusion-based three-dimensional spatial field prediction method is proposed for real-time CO2 spatial fields’ inference, which integrates spatial mesh regularization, a lightweight main prediction network, and a large model (LM)-driven physical knowledge guidance module. Specifically, spatial mesh regularization is applied to regularize historical spatial fields and ensure structural and scale consistency. The lightweight main prediction network employs the enhanced 3D U-Net to perform feature-level fusion of historical CO2 fields and control parameter tensors, enabling efficient extraction of multi-scale spatial features. A Qwen-7B-based LM provides decision-level fusion through supervision and physical-knowledge-guided assessment of key regional behaviors. Furthermore, the comprehensive spatial field metrics are established to enable evaluation-level fusion of key regional statistics and spatial distributions, providing a quantitative assessment of field prediction performance. Experiments across different operating conditions show that the method improves the overall prediction accuracy by approximately 10% compared with GCN, enhances prediction stability in key regions by 3%-10%, and reduces computation time by 98.3% relative to CFD.

items.title: Auxiliary diagnosis of depression in youth based on 3D-CBSResNet12 and multi-modal fusion strategy
items.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a mental illness with a significantly higher prevalence, especially among the youth population. In recent years, with the continuous innovation of deep learning technologies, the combination of medical imaging and computer-aided diagnosis has opened up new avenues and possibilities for studying a variety of diseases. However, many challenges are still faced in the research for the disease of depression. Among them, how to effectively improve the performance of network models under the condition of limited and small datasets is an urgent and crucial topic. Therefore, this paper proposes an auxiliary diagnosis method for depression, combining a lightweight deep learning network and a multi-modal feature fusion strategy, aiming to achieve more accurate and efficient depression diagnosis. Specifically, a lightweight dual-path architecture called 3D-CBSResNet12 is constructed, which utilizes multiple effective convolutional approaches as its core operations and employs a multi-modal feature fusion strategy to achieve more comprehensive and accurate classification of depression. Experimental results show that 3D-CBSResNet12 achieves significant performance improvement, fully validating its feasibility and effectiveness.

items.title: Beyond bi-temporal and unimodal: A multimodal-temporal coupling network for change detection in conflict zones
items.abstract: Practical and accurate building damage assessment in conflict zones is a critical yet challenging task for humanitarian aid and post-event recovery. Conventional change detection methods, however, are often constrained by the bi-temporal, homogeneous data assumption, failing to synergistically leverage multimodal pre-event references and dense, all-weather post-event observations. Our second contribution is the proposal of the Multimodal-Temporal Coupling Network (MTCNet), a unified framework designed to explicitly model this complex data environment. MTCNet features a dual-branch architecture that synergistically couples a bi-temporal, multimodal comparison stream with a temporal analysis stream. Its core innovations include a Change-aware Alignment (CAA) module to bridge the modality gap and a Spatio-Temporal Attention Differentiation (STAD) module that enriches difference features with deep temporal context from the Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) sequence. Extensive experiments on the M2Change benchmark demonstrate that MTCNet substantially outperforms a wide range of state-of-the-art bi-temporal, multimodal, and time-series change detection methods, establishing a new performance benchmark. items.title: BuildingCD-Mamba: An efficient shuffle-scan mamba with temporal-spatial feature fusion for urban building change detection
items.abstract: Building change detection (BCD) is a fundamental yet challenging task in remote sensing, requiring precise localization of subtle structural changes from multi-temporal, high-resolution imagery. Despite recent progress, existing convolutional networks lack the capacity to capture long-range dependencies, whereas Transformer-based alternatives impose prohibitive quadratic computational burdens. Furthermore, conventional feature extractors often sacrifice high-frequency boundary details in complex urban scenes, while standard sequence modeling lacks an efficient mechanism to focus on sparse, change-prone regions across large-scale imagery. To address these issues, we propose BuildingCD-Mamba, a novel deep learning framework that integrates state space modeling into BCD tasks and introduces three key innovations: (1) a wavelet-based feature decomposition strategy that separately processes low- and high-frequency components to enhance edge sensitivity while preserving structural details; (2) a Shuffle State Space Module with a coarse-to-fine scanning mechanism that prioritizes high-change regions for efficient and accurate feature propagation; and (3) a Temporal-Spatial Feature Fusion module designed to comprehensively integrate multi-scale temporal and spatial cues. Extensive experiments on five widely used benchmark datasets demonstrate that BuildingCD-Mamba consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in F1-score, IoU, and overall accuracy, achieving superior boundary delineation and robustness in detecting small-scale changes. The proposed framework bridges advances in state space modeling and multi-source feature fusion, offering a scalable solution for urban monitoring.

items.title: CausalCEM: Self-improved causal counterfactual emotion modeling for multimodal physiological signals
items.abstract: Multimodal physiological signals originating from the central and autonomic nervous systems (CNS/ANS) hold unique advantages for emotion recognition. However, existing methods struggle to effectively model the inter-system and temporal synergy inherent in these heterogeneous signals. Furthermore, existing neural models are typically opaque, hindering the interpretation of underlying causal dependencies and the prediction of intervention outcomes. To address these challenges, we propose Causal Counterfactual Emotion Modeling (CausalCEM), a novel self-improved framework for multimodal physiological signal-based emotion recognition. CausalCEM achieves the research goal of revealing underlying neural system synergy mechanisms and enhancing model interpretability and robustness by unifying causal discovery and counterfactual reasoning to drive the physiological emotion recognition process. Specifically, we formulate the physiological generation process as a Structural Causal Model (SCM) to uncover the directed causal topology and quantitative influence among CNS and ANS variables. Guided by this structure, we introduce a Causal-Informed Temporal Gated Network (CITGN) that fuses causal priors with temporal dynamics for robust prediction. Furthermore, we devise a Physiological-constraint Counterfactual (PhysCF) phase to generate plausible counterfactual samples via topology-guided interventions, driving a self-improved training strategy to iteratively refine the framework. This continuous regularization forces the model to adhere to underlying physiological causality, effectively mitigating reliance on spurious correlations. Experimental results demonstrate that CausalCEM significantly improves emotion recognition performance by effectively modeling the underlying causal synergy and facilitating counterfactual prediction.

items.title: Collaborative learning for unsupervised multimodal image registration: Integrating self-supervision and MIM-guided diffusion-based image translation
items.abstract: The substantial variations in radiometric, texture, and structural characteristics pose significant challenges for the accurate registration of multimodal images. While supervised deep learning methods have demonstrated strong performance, they often rely on large-scale annotated datasets, limiting their practical application. Traditional unsupervised methods usually optimize registration by minimizing differences in feature representations, yet frequently fail to robustly capture geometric discrepancies, particularly under substantial spatial and radiometric variations. To address these challenges, we propose a Collaborative Learning framework for Unsupervised Multimodal Image Registration, named CoLReg, which reformulates unsupervised registration learning into a collaborative training paradigm comprising three components: (1) a cross-modal image translation network, MIMGCD, which employs a learnable Maximum Index Map (MIM) guided conditional diffusion model to generate image pairs that have modality-consistent with real unsupervised cross-modal image pairs; (2) a self-supervised intermediate registration network which learns to estimate geometric transformations using synthetic cross-modal image pairs with accurate displacement labels ; (3) a distilled cross-modal registration network trained with pseudo-labels predicted by the intermediate network. The three networks are jointly optimized through an alternating training strategy wherein each network enhances the performance of the others. This mutual collaboration progressively reduces modality discrepancies, enhances the quality of pseudo-labels, and improves registration accuracy. Extensive experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that our CoLReg achieves competitive or superior performance compared to state-of-the-art unsupervised approaches (e.g., Alto, SCPNet, SSHNet, and SSHNet-D) and even surpasses several supervised baselines (e.g., DHN, MHN, and ReDFeat).

items.title: DLBN: A deep logic belief network for fault diagnosis of dust removal fans
items.abstract: Accurate and interpretable fan fault diagnosis is essential for ensuring safety and environmental compliance in steelmaking workshops. Although Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have shown high accuracy, their black-box nature limits practical deployment. Currently, researchers are increasingly focusing on logic extraction from DNNs to produce a semantic understanding of DNN-based fan diagnostic decision-making. Thus, this paper develops a Deep Logic Belief Network (DLBN) which unifies symbolic reasoning at both the feature and decision levels so as to visualize DNN’s feature learning and reasoning for diagnostic decision-making. In the DLBN, two symbolic rules (M-of-N and KAL) are designed to interpret how stacked Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) work and generate a nonlinear mathematical representation for decision boundaries of fan diagnostic decision-making, respectively. Specifically, to derive M-of-N rules, a novel RBM is designed to reduce network information loss (i.e., ensure the activation status of the hidden units will not change during logic extraction). Besides, based on the Kolmogorov–Arnold theorem, a novel structure, Kolmogorov Spline Networks, is designed to generate a nonlinear decision boundary (KAL rules). The two modules are seamlessly integrated to enable a coherent explanation pipeline. Finally, experimental results on three datasets (fan testbed, industrial fan, and public bearing datasets) demonstrate that DLBN outperforms several latest baseline models in diagnostic performance and interpretability. DLBN demonstrates practical value in optimizing prior diagnostic rules by aligning better with domain knowledge, achieving a 6.3% higher 𝐹1 score through its nonlinear mapping capability. These findings suggest that DLBN offers a promising approach for transparent and deployable intelligent fault diagnosis in complex industrial environments.

items.title: Decoding depression: A hybrid GRU–Mamba architecture with multi-dimensional interpretability framework for facial dynamics analysis
items.abstract: Traditional depression assessment still relies on clinical interviews and self-report scales. These tools are widely used, but they often suffer from limited access to trained clinicians, inconsistent ratings between examiners, and a lack of objective indicators of symptom severity. To ease these problems, we propose a Hybrid GRU-Mamba model that detects depression from facial dynamics and offers a non-invasive alternative that does not depend on long questionnaires. Short-term facial changes are described by one-dimensional convolutions, medium-range patterns are learned by bidirectional GRUs, and long-range emotional trends are modeled by lightweight Mamba state-space blocks that handle long sequences with nearly linear cost. An attention-based pooling layer then fuses these multi-scale features so that the network can focus on subtle facial cues related to depressive states. To make the model more transparent, a cross-dimensional explanation framework is added. It summarizes model behavior through five views: spatial importance, temporal significance, temporal evolution, region interaction, and stability under small perturbations. In this way, it is possible to observe weakened coordination between facial regions and irregular timing in expressive changes that match clinical impressions. Experiments were conducted on a clinically validated dataset of 90 participants (801 video clips) collected at the Shanghai Mental Health Center. Under a subject-independent evaluation protocol, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 81.0% and a macro-F1 score of 80.0% at the clip level. When predictions are aggregated at the subject level, performance increases to 87.1% accuracy and 86.8% macro-F1. Additional evaluations indicate that these results are stable across different subject partitions. Overall, the model provides competitive depression detection performance together with clinically meaningful explanations, which may support more reliable and interpretable AI-assisted assessment.

items.title: Decoding emotional nuances: A multimodal approach to detecting depression through audio, video, and text
items.abstract: Early detection of depression is crucial to prevent serious consequences, such as chronic fatigue, substance abuse, and worsening mental health. Traditional diagnostic methods often rely on self-reported questionnaires, which can be influenced by a patient’s willingness to disclose information, or on unimodal approaches that may not capture the full range of depressive symptoms. To address these limitations, we present LUNA (Listen, Understand, Nurture, Advise), a unified multimodal application-based framework designed to emulate real-world mental health assessments by integrating video, audio, and text inputs. LUNA employs individual modules for each modality, combining their results to provide a comprehensive analysis of the user’s mental state. Our findings show that each module can independently and effectively screen for depression, and their combined scores yield a more comprehensive and accurate regression score based on the PHQ-8 scale for each user session. Benchmarking against state-of-the-art depression detection models using the DAIC-WOZ dataset demonstrates that LUNA performs comparably to or better than existing validated models. To ensure privacy, no user data is stored post-assessment. Furthermore, the system features an interactive avatar to enhance user engagement and comfort. LUNA represents a significant advancement in the early detection of depression by providing a robust, privacy-conscious and user-friendly diagnostic tool.

items.abstract: The high prevalence of retinal diseases has made early diagnosis a critical focus in ophthalmology research. Furthermore, we propose a cross-modal Mamba fusion (CMMF) module that integrates a loose pairwise training strategy with an adaptive dynamic weighting mechanism to optimize modality contributions. This module leverages Mamba-based alignment to enhance fusion efficiency and overall diagnostic performance. Extensive experiments on challenging benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in accurately diagnosing a wide range of retinal diseases. items.title: Diagnostically faithful fMRI-dMRI synthesis using disease-informed diffusion priors
items.abstract: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) are vital for studying Alzheimer’s disease but often suffer from missing modalities. Existing generative models fail to capture the fundamental signal mismatch between fMRI and dMRI or incorporate disease-relevant anatomy, yielding diagnostically weak outputs. We propose Pattern-aware Diffusion Synthesis (PDS), a pattern-aware diffusion framework that integrates structure-function coupling priors from anatomical atlases into a dual-modal 3D diffusion model, enabling semantically coherent bidirectional synthesis. A tissue-aware projection network and microstructure refinement module further enhance anatomical fidelity. Experiments on OASIS-3, ADNI, and an in-house cohort show PDS achieves state-of-the-art PSNR/SSIM: 29.83 dB/0.908 (fMRI) and 30.00 dB/0.776 (dMRI). Crucially, synthetic scans support robust diagnosis: using hybrid real-synthetic data, PDS yields 67.92% accuracy in normal control (NC)/ mild cognitive impairment (MCI)/Alzheimer’s disease (AD) classification; when trained only on synthetic data and tested on real scans, it achieves 77.35% accuracy-the highest among all methods-demonstrating superior preservation of clinically meaningful information.

items.title: Diffusion-based frequency degradation prior fusion with hierarchical wavelet decompositions for underwater image enhancement
items.abstract: Underwater image enhancement (UIE) aims to restore clear images from degraded underwater scenes. Although diffusion model-based methods have achieved remarkable results, they often require excessive denoising steps, leading to low computational efficiency. To address this, we propose FPG-Diff, a novel UIE framework that integrates frequency prior guidance from a diffusion model with hierarchical wavelet-domain enhancement through a cross-domain fusion strategy. Specifically, a Frequency-domain Diffusion Model (FDM) is designed to generate latent degradation priors that capture the frequency characteristics of underwater degradation. These priors then guide and fuse with a Wavelet-space Hierarchical Enhancement Network (WHENet), which separately enhances high-frequency and low-frequency sub-bands. Within WHENet, a High-frequency Dilated Attention Module (HDAM) combines multi-scale dilated convolutions and self-attention to refine textures, while a Frequency Prior Fusion Guided Module (FPFGM) fuses the generated priors with amplitude components of the low-frequency sub-band in the frequency domain to guide the restoration of degraded information. Since the latent degradation prior is formulated as a compact representation, the FDM requires only a few denoising iterations to generate accurate target values, thereby significantly improving the overall model efficiency. Extensive experiments conducted on public benchmark datasets demonstrate that FPG-Diff achieves superior enhancement performance compared with state-of-the-art methods. items.title: Diffusion-prior based implicit neural representation for arbitrary-scale cardiac cine MRI super-resolution
items.abstract: Cardiac cine MRI enables dynamic visualization of cardiac motion and provides functional measurements. However, its resolution is often constrained by acquisition window limitations and motion artifacts. Existing super-resolution methods often rely on fixed up-sampling scales, limiting their flexibility to meet diverse imaging requirements. While standard diffusion models have shown strong capabilities in image enhancement, they suffer from lengthy inference times and limited control over detail generation. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel diffusion-prior based implicit neural representation (DP-INR) for arbitrary-scale cine MRI super-resolution. DP-INR effectively combines the prior information learning capabilities of diffusion models with the global information integration capacity of spatio-temporal implicit attention. Specifically, reference frame features extracted by an encoder serve as temporal context information, guiding the diffusion model’s decoding process of target frame latent features. This approach effectively constrains the inherent uncertainty in latent features during diffusion, thereby enhancing the model’s ability to generate fine cardiac details. Subsequently, spatial-aware implicit attention decodes spatial coordinates to produce high-resolution images, while temporal-aware implicit attention facilitates motion estimation. By incorporating diffusion models into implicit neural representations, DP-INR generates high-quality priors with only a few time steps, thereby avoiding the time-consuming iterative optimization process of conventional diffusion models. Experiments on both in-house and public datasets demonstrate that DP-INR outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations, highlighting its efficacy in improving the resolution of cardiac cine MRI.

items.abstract: Depression is a prevalent psychiatric condition, affecting nearly 280 million individuals worldwide. Traditional approaches to diagnosing and treating depression are often highly subjective, lacking objective and effective methods for accurate recognition and non-pharmacological interventions. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework for depression recognition and intervention that integrates multimodal physiological signals with large language models (LLMs). Next, we design a multimodal alignment module that leverages Cross-Modal Attention (CMA) and LLMs architectures to enable deep fusion of heterogeneous physiological data. During the intervention phase, additional modalities such as text and speech are incorporated to enhance user interaction, enabling personalized and intelligent monitoring of dynamic psychological states and the generation of closed-loop, negative-feedback-based intervention strategies. Through comprehensive multimodal data collection and systematic experimental validation, our results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional approaches in terms of signal reconstruction quality, depression recognition accuracy, and intervention efficacy. This study offers a novel technical pathway and theoretical foundation for the early detection and intelligent intervention of depression, demonstrating substantial scientific value and application potential.

items.title: Emotion recognition using multimodal physiological signals through regional to global fusion with a spatial-temporal semantic alignment mechanism
items.abstract: With the continuous development of multimodal learning, emotion recognition using multimodal physiological signals has become a research hotspot. Studies have shown that combining electroencephalogram (EEG) signals and eye movements can significantly improve the results of emotion recognition. However, current research still faces the following challenges: (1) Individuals’ response times and durations to different emotions vary, leading to data diversity and variability. (2) Different modalities exhibit spatiotemporal discrepancies, which may result in varying semantic relevance and significance under the same spatiotemporal conditions. To address these challenges, we propose a Regional to Global Fusion Network with a Spatial-Temporal Semantic Alignment Mechanism (R2GFANet). Initially, R2GFANet addresses the first challenge by employing padding masks in conjunction with a 1D-CNN network to encode temporal semantic information from variable-length EEG signals and eye movements. Subsequently, R2GFANet leverages a Multi-Region Cross-Modal Attention mechanism for parallel temporal semantic alignment within each brain region and applies region-level spatial attention to highlight the semantic information of critical brain regions, effectively addressing spatiotemporal discrepancies across modalities. By comparing our method with numerous state-of-the-art approaches on two public datasets, SEED-IV and SEED-V, we demonstrate the outstanding performance and statistical significance of the proposed R2GFANet. Additionally, we conduct ablation studies and visualization analyses. The results indicate that aligning EEG signals with eye movements not only improves classification performance but also provides neuroscientific interpretability.

items.title: Emotional lateralization-inspired spatiotemporal neural networks for EEG-based emotion recognition
items.abstract: Due to the volume conduction effects of the brain, multi-channel electroencephalogram (EEG) contains redundant information, potentially causing overfitting problems and increasing the computational cost. For that, EEG channel selection solutions based on correlation analysis or supervised learning have been investigated to ascertain the vital channels in the EEG emotion recognition task. However, these studies may tend to overfit high-frequency emotions due to supervised learning channel selection and underfit low-frequency ones, thus performing poorly. Hence, it is an essential issue to select an effective channel subset without supervised guidance to represent the universal emotional status. In this paper, we propose a channel selection method named emotional lateralization-inspired spatiotemporal neural networks (ELSTNN) for EEG emotion recognition. In ELSTNN, the neuroscience finding of emotional lateralization is applied to guide channel selection with unsupervised learning, thereby removing redundant channels and preserving the lateralization phenomenon. For emotion recognition, ELSTNN employs three convolution layers and one long short-term memory layer to mine and integrate the deep spatiotemporal features from the selected EEG signals. Extensive experiments are carried out on public DEAP and DREAMER datasets, which show that ELSTNN outperforms various state-of-the-art methods with statistical significance (p < 0.05) in both datasets, achieving the average accuracy of 95.67 % in valence and 94.97 % in arousal on DEAP, and 93.72 % in valence and 93.57 % in arousal on DREAMER. It demonstrates that our proposed ELSTNN chooses the channel that is more universally applicable since it preserves the basic emotional lateralization with more universal applicability to various emotions.

items.abstract: Major depressive disorder is projected to become the leading contributor to mental illness by 2030. While resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) has emerged as a non-invasive solution for depression detection, two significant challenges remain. First, due to medical data privacy regulations and the high costs associated with acquiring the necessary equipment, individual medical institutions struggle to obtain sufficient annotated data. Specifically, a federated learning architecture ensures both physical data isolation and patient privacy through parameter aggregation. A state-space model-based Mamba network captures cross-modal correlations between fMRI time-series features and non-imaging features. items.title: Hybrid long-range feature fusion network for multi-modal waste semantic segmentation
items.abstract: Efficient waste recycling not only helps to achieve resource reuse, but also alleviates environmental pollution. Compared to inefficient manual sorting methods, waste recycling solutions based on computer vision play a more important role. It not only improves work efficiency, but also reduces labor costs. However, most methods only use traditional color images to achieve waste segmentation, which makes it unsuitable for complex scenes. To fully exploit the benefits of multi-modal data, this paper proposes a novel hybrid long-range feature fusion network (HLRFF-Net) based on Transformer and Mamba architectures for multi-modal waste semantic segmentation. It introduces additional hyperspectral images as auxiliary information to further improve waste segmentation performance in cluttered scenes. On the one hand, we develop a novel cross fusion module (CFM) based on the agent attention mechanism to process multi-modal features, which can effectively achieve mutual guidance and feature enhancement by modeling long-range dependencies. On the other hand, we design an effective semantic refinement module (SRM) based on multi-scale perception to provide more discriminative features for multi-modal waste segmentation. It not only introduces a long-range enhancement module (LREM) to capture global contextual features, but also utilizes a short-range enhancement module (SREM) to capture local detail features. In addition, it also uses a channel attention module (CAM) to enhance important feature maps. To further verify the effectiveness of our model, we conduct relevant experiments on two representative multi-modal image datasets. Experimental results show that our method is not only applicable to different application scenarios, but also more competitive compared to other semantic segmentation models.

items.title: Identifying spatial domains from spatial multi-omics data using consistent and specific deep subspace learning
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of spatial omics technologies has revolutionized the ability to simultaneously capture multi-omics data along with spatial information, offering unprecedented insights into tissue architecture and cellular heterogeneity. Spatial domain identification is a fundamental step in spatial omics analysis, as it facilitates the delineation of functional tissue regions. However, most existing methods are tailored for single omic data and face substantial limitations when extended to spatial multi-omics contexts. Integrating consistent and complementary signals across multiple omics within spatially structured data remains a key challenge. In this study, we propose SpaMICS, a deep subspace learning framework designed for spatial domain identification from spatial multi-omics data. SpaMICS captures spatial dependencies and latent inter-spot relationships to learn high-level representations for each omic. To enhance information integration, we introduce a subspace learning module that explicitly disentangles consistent and complementary information across omics. Furthermore, we incorporate dual constraints to enhance information extraction: a low-rank constraint to emphasize consistent information across omics and a discriminative constraint that facilitates the extraction of complementary information. Extensive experiments on five real-world spatial multi-omics datasets, including spatial transcriptomics–proteomics and spatial transcriptomics–epigenomics data, demonstrate that SpaMICS consistently outperforms existing approaches, effectively integrating multi-omics data for accurate spatial domain identification.

items.title: Learning multimodal representations for incomplete EHRs with retrieval-augmented personalized modality recovery
items.abstract: As Electronic Health Records (EHRs) proliferate, multimodal methods become increasingly valuable for clinical prediction. However, missing modalities lead to modality imbalance and degraded fusion performance. Recovering missing modalities has emerged as an effective way to mitigate this issue. Despite this, existing recovery strategies neither efficiently use globally similar conditions as modal-unique priors nor fuse them with the patient’s own available modality, leading to the loss of patient-specific information. To fill these gaps, we propose RAMCare, a two-step missing modality recovery framework that combines retrieval-augmented priors and mixture-of-experts offset modeling for incomplete EHR representation learning, which is realized by a three-stage training process: (1) a Relevant Case Retrieval Augmented Module that builds a global case library of cross-modal aligned condition pairs via co-clustering, enabling efficient retrieval of condition-matched modal-unique priors for preliminary recovery; (2) a Mixture of Experts Offset Module that selects condition experts based on retrieved weights and patient-specific features, mapping the retrieved deviation to personalized offsets of the missing modality to capture individual variation and refine the recovery; (3) a finetuning stage that further enhances recovery and multimodal fusion performance. Evaluated on two real-world datasets with missing modalities, RAMCare achieves state-of-the-art performance.

items.title: MB-DDPM: microbiome simulation based on the denoising diffusion probabilistic model
items.abstract: The rapid development of metagenomics has revealed the close associations between the microbiome and human diseases, and a large number of statistical methods have been developed for metagenomic analysis. The development of statistical models usually requires simulated data experiments to evaluate the performance of the methods, while the generation of simulated data becomes a key step in conducting such experiments. However, existing methods for simulated data generation fail to capture the complex characteristics of microbiome data. In this study, we propose a novel microbiome simulation framework based on the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (MB-DDPM), which is capable of fitting the intrinsic structure of real microbial communities. The model is trained using given real microbiome data during the diffusion process to retain transformation parameters. Then, the model uses these parameters to gradually transform the randomly sampled standard Gaussian distribution data into a simulated dataset via the back propagation process. MB-DDPM employs a U-Net-based architecture that effectively captures the complex characteristics of microbial communities, including species abundance distribution, microbial interaction relationships, and community dynamics. As a deep learning-based approach, MB-DDPM does not require any distribution assumptions for microbiome data. Our experiments demonstrate that MB-DDPM outperforms existing methods in multiple critical indicators, including Shannon diversity index, Simpson diversity index, Spearman correlation, and proportional analysis. MB-DDPM not only enhances the biological plausibility of generated data but also provides high-quality simulated data for microbiome research, facilitating ecological analysis and disease-associated studies.
